annotations.title: Look an Old English word up

description:
Look an Old English word up on Wiktionary and return its senses plus full
declension/conjugation tables — attested content, not invented. Any form of
the word works; an inflected query is resolved to its lemma automatically
via previously cached paradigms and the result notes the resolution. With
search_language='eng' the query is a modern English word instead: the
result lists its per-sense Old English equivalents (the translations block)
plus their expanded entries. Returns Markdown plus the same result as
structuredContent matching the declared outputSchema.

Results are cached server-side; first-time queries reach the live upstream
politely and calls are rate limited — on a rate-limit error, wait a few
seconds and retry. Content is from en.wiktionary.org (CC BY-SA 4.0 —
attribute and share alike if republished).

SearchLanguage.description:
The query language. ``ang`` looks an Old English word up directly (any of
its forms — an inflected query resolves via cached paradigms). ``eng`` searches
in reverse: the English Wiktionary page for the query word lists per-sense Old
English translations, and each distinct lemma is then looked up normally.
SearchLanguage.title: SearchLanguage

include_forms.description: When true (default), each match's full declension/conjugation table is returned INLINE — usable cases/tenses (nouns, the adjectives' strong/weak family, the verbs' moods, the pronouns' dual) in ONE call, no follow-up anglo_get_inflections. Set false for a cheap screen of which entries exist. Bounded by a per-search cap — use max_forms to adjust per call. For eng queries this governs the expanded Old English entries; the per-sense translations list itself is always returned.
include_forms.title: Include Forms

max_forms.description: Optional override for how many inflection tables to expand this call (0–12). On an uncached query each table is one politely paced upstream fetch, so high values on cold queries are slow. Omit for the server default.
max_forms.title: Max Forms

query.description: The word to look up, in the language search_language names. Old English (default): a SINGLE Old English word, any form — an inflected form ('bindaþ') is resolved to its lemma ('bindan') automatically via cached paradigms, and the result says so; the special letters are optional once a paradigm is cached ('thing' finds þing, 'waeter' finds wæter). English (search_language='eng'): the English word whose Old English equivalents you want — multiword entries like 'apple tree' work.
query.title: Query

search_language.description: Language the query word is in: 'ang' (default) looks the Old English word up directly; 'eng' finds the Old English equivalents of a modern English word (per-sense, from Wiktionary's translation tables) and returns their full entries. Glosses are in modern English either way.

name: anglo_search

AngloNominalParadigm.description:
Declension of a noun/adjective/pronoun: case key → {singular, dual, plural}.

Noun tables are plain: the bare case is the key ('nominative', 'genitive',
'instrumental'). Adjective tables split by gender (suffixed: 'nominative
feminine') and come one per declension class (strong/weak), folded in as a
title-derived prefix: 'strong nominative feminine', 'weak dative neuter'.
The personal-pronoun table splits by person (and, in the third person, gender)
and carries the dual: 'first person nominative' → {singular, dual, plural},
'third person masculine accusative' → {singular, …, plural}. ``category``
discriminates this from the verbal and not-found shapes — switch on it before
reading the body.

cases.description: Case key (lower-case: 'nominative', 'genitive', 'instrumental', …) → its singular/dual/plural forms, in table order. Adjectives prefix the declension class and suffix the gender ('strong nominative feminine'); pronouns prefix the person and, in the third person, the gender ('first person nominative', 'third person masculine accusative'). ``dual`` is populated only on pronoun cells.
cases.title: Cases

source.default: Wiktionary, the free dictionary (en.wiktionary.org), Old English entries. Wikimedia Foundation. AngloNominalParadigm.title: AngloNominalParadigm

AngloNumberForms.description:
A declension cell: the number forms of one case key. Forms are verbatim
normalized Old English; alternates stay comma-separated as Wiktionary renders
them. A number the table doesn't give is an empty string — ``dual`` is filled
only by the personal-pronoun paradigm (nouns and adjectives have no dual).
AngloNumberForms.title: AngloNumberForms

AngloVerbalParadigm.description:
Conjugation of a verb, grouped the way Wiktionary's tables are: finite cells
keyed by mood and tense → person-and-number → form, plus the non-finite forms
(the two infinitives and the participles). Old English verbs are active only —
there is no mediopassive voice — so all finite keys are bare.

finite.description: Mood and tense (lower-case: 'indicative present', 'subjunctive past'; the imperative has no tense — its key is just 'imperative') → person and number ('first singular' … 'third singular', and the bare 'singular'/'plural' the subjunctive and imperative use) → the form. Alternates are comma-separated; an em-dash cell (no such form) is omitted.
finite.title: Finite

nonfinite.description: Non-finite form ('infinitive', 'inflected infinitive', 'present participle', 'past participle') → {'form': <the form>}.
nonfinite.title: Nonfinite

source.default: Wiktionary, the free dictionary (en.wiktionary.org), Old English entries. Wikimedia Foundation. Entry.description:
One Old English entry on the page: the headword (page title) with one
part-of-speech section's senses.
Entry.title: Entry

InflectionHandle.description:
A structured anchor for fetching a full paradigm: feed ``entry_id`` (the page
title) + ``word_class`` (the POS section) to ``anglo_get_inflections`` — or ask
``search`` to include the table inline (``forms``).

entry_id.description: Wiktionary page title — the lemma itself.
entry_id.title: Entry Id

forms.description: The full paradigm, populated when a search is asked to include forms. None when not requested or beyond the cap.
forms.title: Forms

InflectionHandle.title: InflectionHandle

ParadigmNotFound.description:
No inflection table for this page/POS (no Old English section, no table, or
the page doesn't exist). ``found`` is False and there is no body.

Sense.description: One sense of an entry: the (HTML-stripped) Wiktionary definition line.
Sense.title: Sense

TranslationSense.description: One English sense (a translations table) and the Old English terms it offers.

sense.description: The sense gloss the source table carries.
sense.title: Sense

TranslationTerm.description:
One Old English word a translations table offers for an English sense.
``word`` is the Wiktionary page title (what an ``eng`` search re-searches and
what ``anglo_get_inflections`` needs).

display.description: Rendered form when it differs from the title.
display.title: Display

qualifier.description: Usage qualifier as marked, e.g. 'poetic'; else empty.
qualifier.title: Qualifier

word.description: Wiktionary page title — the lemma itself.
word.title: Word

TranslationTerm.title: TranslationTerm

outputSchema.description: The result of a dictionary search.

forms_truncated.description: How many handles did NOT get an inline table because the per-search cap was reached.
forms_truncated.title: Forms Truncated

found.description: False when nothing matched. For an eng query, True means Old English translations were found — entries may still be empty when none of them could be expanded (see translations).
found.title: Found

resolved_from.description: The original inflected query when resolved; else empty. ang queries only — always empty for eng results.
resolved_from.title: Resolved From

resolved_lemma.description: The lemma actually searched when resolved; else empty. ang queries only — always empty for eng results.
resolved_lemma.title: Resolved Lemma

search_method.description: How the match was found: 'direct' = the query itself matched; 'lemma_index' = an inflected form resolved via a previously cached paradigm; 'translations' = an English query resolved via Wiktionary translation tables.
search_method.title: Search Method
